12.t: Working with data: seat belts and inertia
q: In which test did the dummy move furthest?
Use Newton’s first law to explain why the dummy kept moving.
An object keeps moving at the same speed unless a force acts. The sled stopped, but nothing stopped the dummy at first.
Calculate how many times smaller the force was with a tight belt than with none.
Explain why a loose belt is worse than a tight one.
The dummy moves further and faster before the belt catches it, then stops more suddenly: a larger force (20 kN).
